generation_members.surface_form: Simulating diffusion properties of solid-state electrolytes via a neural network potential: Performance and training scheme
Plasma synthesis of electrolyte nanopowders

Using Materials Project tools, researchers designed a new class of sodium‑based carbonophosphate compounds, predicted them to be thermodynamically stable, synthesized them hydrothermally, and experimentally confirmed their Li‑ion battery performance after ion exchange.

CHGNet molecular dynamics simulations of Li superionic conductors reproduce room‑temperature ionic conductivities and activation energies within the error bars of AIMD, correctly distinguishing faster from slower conductors.
TensorNet‑MatPES predicts ionic conductivities of Li/Na solid electrolytes with high fidelity (positive R²), whereas TensorNet‑MPF severely overestimates conductivities and yields a negative R².
Orb-v3 and SevenNet classify materials as good versus bad ionic conductors with accuracy greater than 82% using a 500 meV migration barrier threshold.
Orb-v3 and SevenNet are suitable for high-throughput screening of candidate battery materials based on their >82% classification accuracy for ionic conductors.

The frozen-framework PES descriptor screening ranks lithium-containing Materials Project compounds such that eight of the ten highest‑ranked materials are confirmed to be room‑temperature superionic conductors by first‑principles calculations.

The DeePMD model successfully reproduces the superionic behavior of solid-state electrolytes with linear Lithium/Sodium mean squared displacement over time and diffusion coefficient uncertainty of about 20% or smaller, which is precise enough for battery applications.
The DeePMD model is a promising candidate for developing a universal potential for solid-state electrolytes, though care must be taken when selecting training configurations.
GNoME-driven molecular dynamics simulations on 623 materials with previously unseen compositions enable classification of unseen compositions as superionic conductors in comparison with AIMD.

M3GNet molecular‑dynamics simulations of Li₃YCl₆ reproduce ionic conductivity (14.3 mS cm⁻¹) and activation energy (0.22 eV) consistent with ab‑initio MD, and short‑time MD correctly identifies known lithium superionic conductors by their high mean‑squared displacements at elevated temperatures.
